title: The Army That Lost A War To Birds
sources: Wikipedia, 'Emu War' (Nov-Dec 1932, Campion district, Western Australia; roughly 20,000 emus; Major G.P.W. Meredith, Royal Australian Artillery, with two Lewis guns and 10,000 rounds; first gun jammed after a handful of kills; Meredith reported 986 emus killed using 9,860 rounds; army withdrew 10 Dec 1932; Meredith's remark that a military division with the bullet-carrying capacity of the emus would face any army in the world)

National Museum of Australia / Australian War Memorial summaries of the 1932 'Emu War' (WWI veterans on Soldier Settlement farms, wheat crops destroyed, ex-servicemen farmers asked for machine guns, Minister for Defence Sir George Pearce approved the operation)
ABC News Australia and Smithsonian Magazine retrospectives on the Emu War (emus split into small groups, the truck could not keep pace over rough ground, farmers later used a bounty scheme)

titles: The Army That Lost A War To Birds

metadata.description: In 1932 the Australian army went to war against 20,000 emus... and the emus won. This is the true story of the Great Emu War. #shorts #history #emuwar #weirdhistory #australia

lines.text: In nineteen thirty-two, the Australian army went to war against twenty thousand emus.
lines.caps: In 1932, | the Australian | army | went to war | against | 20,000 | emus.

lines.text: And the emus won.
See, after World War One, Australia gave farmland to war veterans,
who started growing wheat.
Then twenty thousand hungry emus showed up,
and destroyed the crops.
The farmers had fought in the war, so they asked for machine guns.
And the army came, with two guns and ten thousand bullets.
lines.caps: And the army | came, | with | two guns | and | 10,000 | bullets.

lines.text: Easy mission, right?
Wrong.
The emus split into tiny groups,
and sprinted away faster than the army's truck.
The first machine gun jammed.
A month later, ten thousand bullets
had taken down only about a thousand emus.
lines.caps: had taken | down | only | about | a thousand | emus.

lines.text: So the army gave up, and went home.
Even the major admitted, if his soldiers could take bullets like these birds,
they could take on any army on Earth.
Final score:
emus one, army zero.
